question: Two students appeared in an examination. One of them secured 9 marks more than the other and his marks were 56% of the sum of their marks. The marks obtained by them were:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **total marks** of both students be 100%.

One student secured **56%** of the total, so the other secured 100% − 56% = **44%**.

Difference in percentage = 56% − 44% = **12%**.

Given difference = **9 marks**. ∴ 12% ≡ 9 marks → 1% = 0.75 marks.

Marks are: 56 × 0.75 = **42** and 44 × 0.75 = **33**.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 and 33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Difference between marks = **9**. Higher marks = **56%** of the sum of marks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/37def73ff14247d6efbdafaba00faf71063c731c65a24d3d8a88ef5cb0c323b2.png] 

Let the marks obtained by the two students be **x** and **(x − 9)**.

According to the question:

⇒ x = 56% of [x + (x − 9)]

⇒ x = 0.56 × (2x − 9)

⇒ x = 1.12x − 5.04

⇒ 1.12x − x = 5.04

⇒ 0.12x = 5.04

⇒ x = 5.04 ÷ 0.12 = 504 ÷ 12

⇒ x = **42**

Marks of the second student = 42 − 9 = **33**.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 and 33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To simplify calculations, convert 56% to a fraction: 56/100 = 14/25. This means if the sum is 25 units, the marks are 14 units.

Ratio Method

If Student A gets 56 units and the sum is 100, the ratio of marks A:B is 56:(100 − 56) = 56:44 = 14:11. Difference = 3 units = 9 marks, so 1 unit = 3 marks.

Linear Equations

Always define the variable based on the total sum or the larger value to keep the multiplication factors positive and manageable.</p
